en.title: Jeon Do-yeon's Oscar Buzz for 'Possible Love' Ignites Global Korean Cinema Conversation
en.summary: Veteran actress Jeon Do-yeon is a frontrunner for an Oscar nomination with her performance in Lee Chang-dong's 'Possible Love.' The film's selection as South Korea's Academy Awards submission and critical acclaim suggest a monumental moment for Korean cinema on the world stage.
en.body:
The global cinematic landscape is abuzz with the possibility of **Jeon Do-yeon** gracing the Academy Awards stage, not just as a nominee, but as a contender for Best Actress. Her powerful performance in **Lee Chang-dong**'s **'Possible Love'** has propelled the film to become South Korea's official submission for the 2027 Best International Feature Film Oscar. This isn't merely a national honor; it's a significant marker in the ever-expanding global reach of Korean storytelling.

**'Possible Love'** delves into the complex lives of two couples: a laid-off worker and his wife, and a documentary filmmaker and her husband. As their paths cross for a documentary project, hidden desires and starkly different realities come to the fore. **Jeon Do-yeon** plays Mi-ok, a woman quietly worn down by hardship, whose performance is being hailed as deeply resonant. Critics have lauded her ability to convey profound emotional depth, particularly the paradoxical nature of finding pain even in moments of joy. The film's intricate screenplay and **Jeon**'s multilayered portrayal are seen as key to its potential to transcend language barriers and connect with international audiences.

## A New Era for Korean Cinema

The international recognition for **Jeon Do-yeon**, who previously made history by winning Best Actress at Cannes for **Lee Chang-dong**'s **'Secret Sunshine'** in 2007, signals a profound shift. While Korean actors were less known globally two decades ago, today their presence is undeniable. **Jeon** herself has pondered how this evolution should influence her artistic choices, concluding that her core drive remains the same: a deep-seated 'greater thirst' for compelling stories. The anticipation surrounding **'Possible Love'** and **Jeon**'s performance suggests that the world is ready for more than just the sensational; it's craving the deeply human, expertly told.

> "Most Korean actors are far better known around the world today than when Jeon Do-yeon won best actress at Cannes for Lee Chang-dong’s ‘Secret Sunshine’ in 2007, becoming the first Korean actress to do so."

This sentiment, echoed in discussions surrounding **'Possible Love'**, highlights the journey Korean cinema has undertaken. The film's selection as the Oscar submission and the subsequent buzz around **Jeon**'s performance are being seen by domestic critics as a distinct moment, different from previous submissions. The emphasis on **Jeon**'s central role as a narrator and her nuanced portrayal of a woman grappling with societal pressures and internal conflict is particularly noted. Her ability to depict a character who, despite enduring hardship, harbors complex feelings of superiority towards those who haven't experienced similar struggles, showcases a remarkable depth that resonates universally.

## What's Next

With **Netflix** set to release **'Possible Love'** globally on November 6, anticipation is building. The streaming giant's involvement, coupled with a dedicated Oscar campaign for **Jeon Do-yeon** and other potential categories, positions the film for significant international exposure. The critical praise from outlets like the Los Angeles Times, which declared it the best film of the year, further solidifies its Oscar prospects and promises a must-watch cinematic event for fans worldwide.
